title: Content hashes are not canonical for map-like model objects
reasoning: canonicalJson is documented as deterministic and feeds the content-addressed model hash, but JSON.stringify preserves object insertion order. Two equivalent spreadsheet models with the same cells inserted in different orders produce different hashes, causing identical content to be stored as a new version and defeating no-op detection.
reproduction: Commit a spreadsheet model whose cells object was built as A1 then B1, then commit the same sheet and values with the cells object built as B1 then A1. The JSON strings and model hashes differ even though the logical model is identical.
recommendation: Use a stable serializer that sorts object keys for map-like objects such as cells while preserving meaningful array order for blocks, sheets, slides, rows, and shapes.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The content-addressing test reuses the same parsed model object, so it never varies insertion order for semantically identical model data.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a core store/model test that asserts canonicalJson and SnapshotStore.commit treat two spreadsheet models with the same cell refs in different object insertion orders as identical.
minimumFixScope: packages/core/src/model/types.ts canonicalJson plus a focused model/store regression test.
